I’d like to propose defining a clear acceptance criteria for each devnet before we move on to the next one. We are progressing very quickly, which is great, but at the moment we seem to be focusing primarily on the happy path before advancing further. We still haven’t achieved stable behavior in multi-subnet tests.

Having explicit acceptance criteria for every devnet run would help us better assess readiness and identify gaps before progressing.

Also, could we please run a few benchmarks on leanMultisig using commodity hardware similar to what we typically use for our devnet runs?

For this, I think we have this tool right? https://bench.leanroadmap.org/

What do instance types such as `n1-standard-4` and `c4-standard-4` represent? Is there a legend or reference document I can look at? I ask because aggregation currently appears to be the primary bottleneck across most client implementations.

Hi everyone, I will not be able to attend today's call.

I would like to provide a development update here for Lantern.

Since last week, we have integrated [c-lean-libp2p](https://github.com/Pier-Two/c-lean-libp2p) into the devnet-4 branch of Lantern and have been busy stabilising it. We have also added integration for Hive tests and plan to release an updated image that will include support for these new tests and c-lean-libp2p.

Given that the devnet-5 specification has been merged, we will focus on implementing it in Lantern to ensure the client can interop when that devnet launches.

Thanks!
